response.markdown_report:
Select a **recent-context-conditioned residual gate** as the next minimal NextItNet experiment. At 20% progress, localized modulation is easier to interpret than simultaneously changing the backbone and objective. Its benefit remains untested.

Three starting insights motivate this choice. First, neutral gate initialization preserves the corrected baseline computation, provided shared tensors are copied explicitly. It preserves the baseline block, not an identity map. Second, current-item conditioning supplies endpoint evidence. A four-item mean adds local composition but cannot reliably distinguish isolated demand from repeated intent. Third, sensitivity differs across categories. CDs’ ordering corruption reduced diagnostic HR@10 by 0.15625, while Industrial’s endpoint replacement reduced it by 0.1875; these training stress tests favor retaining both pathways, without proving harmful historical dependence.

Three literature insights organize the directions. NextItNet [1] preserves ordered causal context. Consequently, pooled conditioning should supplement its convolutions. Hierarchical Gating Networks and Highway Networks [2,4] establish conditional selection. Novelty therefore concerns this integration, while ReZero and LayerScale [5,6] clarify its different initialization. Sampled-softmax research [3] motivates stronger candidate discrimination. Test that objective separately to preserve attribution.

| Direction | Evidence used | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| Recent-context residual gating | Endpoint and recent embedding composition | Redundancy with existing hidden states |
| Causal tap gating | Source/destination representations | Dependency and masking complexity |
| Multi-negative objective | Training alternative scores | False negatives and temperature sensitivity |

Scores below are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment lists corresponding strengths and weaknesses.

| Proposal | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Recent-context residual gate [1,2,4] | 3/6/7/5/4 | Specific integration; extensible; targets stale weighting and nonspecific matches; permits selective discrimination; localized patch | Established gating; redundant inputs; intent unobserved; sensitivity is not failure proof; export and graph checks required |
| Causal tap gates [1,2] | 5/7/7/6/7 | Finer selection; reusable; targets stale/isolated signals; changes historical access; standard tensor operations | Related selective-memory ideas; optimization risk; intent unknown; no validated gain; invasive convolution changes |
| Multi-negative sampled softmax [3] | 2/6/5/6/4 | Established foundation; portable; strengthens candidate competition; targets poor ranks; unchanged backbone | Little novelty; sampler dependence; weak recency alignment; margins may mislead; collision handling required |

The selected gate adds a masked causal four-item mean to the starting gate, targeting two user failures: older interactions outweighing current interests and broad relevance displacing specific recent matches. It also targets weak candidate separation—Electronics’ clean diagnostic mean rank was 8.75—while retaining useful ordering pathways. These are hypotheses; no measured model defect establishes gating as its remedy.

Initialize its multiplier to one; retain the loss, dilation schedule and optimizer. Compare neutral, learned-static and context-conditioned scaling when budget permits. Mean pooling preserves relative composition, loses order and absolute multiplicity, and often duplicates existing context [7]. Derive all convolution/gate dependencies, verify predictor parity, and interpret patches with downstream embedding paths explicitly acknowledged [8]. Select solely by host macro validation HR@10, deploying one checkpoint per category. Compatibility, ownership and immediate intent remain unobserved.

idea.description: Extend the supplied current-input-item-conditioned NextItNet residual gate with a masked causal mean of the most recent four input item embeddings. For each completed baseline residual update u_t, compute g_t = sigmoid(W[h_t; u_t; e_t; c_t] + b) / sigmoid(2), then return mask_t * (h_t + g_t * u_t). Initialize W=0 and b=2. Each block has its own jointly trained vector gate; all blocks retain the corrected baseline causal convolutions and dilation schedule. The gate initially preserves the baseline block computation, not an identity mapping.
idea.motivation: The local mean supplies explicit recent composition alongside the current item and ordered hidden state. This targets excessive weighting of older or occasional interactions and broad relevance displacing specific recent interests. Repetition changes relative composition, but a mean does not identify absolute repetition, demand or intent: [A,B] and [A,A,B,B] have equal means, and permutations within a full window are indistinguishable to this feature. The current item and NextItNet states retain additional ordering information. Weak diagnostic candidate separation motivates selective representation learning, but training sensitivity does not prove stale-interest errors, shortcut learning or validation gains. Historical ordering must remain available because its corruption substantially degraded CDs diagnostic predictions. At 20% progress, retain this small experiment before pursuing invasive tap gating or a separate multi-negative objective.
idea.implementation_notes:
Architecture and scope: integrate into the supplied corrected baseline rather than reconstructing an unspecified training pipeline. Use a vector gate with output dimension H and Linear(4H,H). Keep baseline residual-dropout placement, normalization, convolution masking, score head, optimizer, sampling and loss unchanged. Define e as the existing input-item embedding before temporal mixing, without an added L2 normalization; define c as its masked causal four-position mean. Neither includes the shifted positive target. Both are jointly trained within the single category network. Preserve full-block B x L x H outputs for diagnostic hooks.

Pooling limitations: c describes local embedding composition, not an ordered sequence or a reliable repetition count. It loses item–position association, spacing and valid-window size; everything before its window is unavailable directly to c. At four valid positions, sum pooling is only four times the mean and adds no information. Mean plus count could expose short-window occupancy, but it is a separate hypothesis and is not silently added to this experiment. Likewise, an ordered four-item projection would be a separate architecture variant. Existing h and u may already encode this local information, making redundancy a central uncertainty. Scaling residual updates cannot remove information already present in h and does not constitute explicit forgetting.

Gate algebra: the multiplier lies in (0, 1/sigmoid(2)), approximately (0,1.1353), allowing stronger suppression than amplification. Its initial derivative with respect to its logit is 1−sigmoid(2), approximately 0.1192; bias two is moderately saturated, not dead. At W=0, gate weights can receive gradients immediately, while conditioning features initially receive no gradient through the gate projection itself. Ordinary residual-branch gradients remain available through the multiplier-one path. This differs from zero-initialized ReZero and near-zero LayerScale; retain bias two to preserve the supplied starting proposal rather than changing initialization concurrently.

Initialization and optimizer: initialize the corrected baseline normally, then register and initialize gates before constructing the optimizer. Use a saved/restored Torch RNG context when creating gates, covering the CPU generator and relevant CUDA generators if construction occurs there, to avoid advancing subsequent baseline randomness. For equivalence checks, explicitly copy every shared baseline tensor into the gated model; equal seeds alone are insufficient. Initialize gates after any generic model initialization pass, or explicitly exclude them from that pass. Compute the denominator using the same dtype/device sigmoid operation as the numerator. Assert that every trainable parameter identity occurs in optimizer parameter groups exactly once. Check finite gradients and actual updates for gate weights and baseline residual parameters on valid training positions; do not require every individual parameter to have nonzero gradients in every batch.

Causality and padding: derive dependency sets from the actual corrected convolution graph rather than inferring them from block names. For stride-one sequential convolution paths, the maximum receptive-field width is 1+sum((k−1)*d), counting every convolution; unions of residual and gate paths determine the full graph, and dilation can leave gaps. At block b, the direct e path contributes offset 0 and c contributes offsets {0,1,2,3}; union these with the dependency sets of h and u. Later convolutions propagate these additions. Do not claim that the four-item gate necessarily increases the final span by exactly three. Use explicit causal left padding d*(k−1), no temporal normalization across future positions, and mask embeddings and intermediate states after biased transformations before further temporal mixing. Keep embedding row zero fixed at zero, exclude padding from loss, and mask completed residual outputs. Perturb future IDs and IDs outside each derived dependency set and require unchanged earlier outputs within declared numerical tolerances. Gradient checks supplement these tests but can miss saturated dependencies.

Controls and selection: the primary experiment changes only the gate conditioning. Before execution, record a finite comparison list and GPU-second allocation using the remaining host budget. Informative controls are fixed neutral scaling, learned per-channel static scaling, the supplied current-item gate, and the proposed recent-context gate. Prioritize the supplied starting gate versus the new gate; run other controls only if allocated budget permits. Independently trained alternatives are experimental comparisons and are never fused or averaged. A static control tests whether conditioning helps beyond adaptive scaling but does not match parameter count; disclose that limitation. Keep each comparison's baseline hyperparameters, validation schedule, checkpoint rule and deterministic tie handling fixed. Do not launch additional objective or architectural variants automatically. No benefit or successful check is claimed here.

Protocol: keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, all four category routes, single-GPU execution, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Honor the host SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200 despite its legacy name. Preserve supplied splits, family-specific sample_batch, evaluator and host checkpoint-selection rule. Every executed training run, diagnostic, debugging step and failure consumes the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; remaining budget is unspecified. Select using pinned host macro validation HR@10 only. Report category results and elapsed compute when measured; do not substitute training diagnostic HR@10, read hidden test data or reuse other trials' checkpoints.

Compatibility and export: preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), and ModelView; view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. Gather features at the maximum nonzero index, never count−1, and retain the baseline explicit empty-history fallback. Store architecture version, gate input/output dimensions, window size, gate normalization constant, corrected baseline architecture configuration and state_dict in each category artifact. Update the embedded predictor writer with identical definitions and integration. Instantiate the actual generated predictor, strictly load the saved state, call eval(), and compare features, candidate scores and rankings with the training model for short, left-padded, full and empty histories supported by the baseline. Check all four routing paths and use declared tolerances for floating-point scores; report any ranking differences, including near ties. Each category loads exactly one independently trained selected checkpoint, without independently fitted scoring components, checkpoint averaging or score fusion.

Diagnostics: retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and metric_definitions. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors. Preserve existing within-event perturbation definitions and rerun numerical controls after the architecture change. Distinguish conditional training sensitivity from host validation. Existing clean/corrupt hidden-state patches leave downstream raw-embedding-to-gate and recent-context-to-gate paths active; they measure a scoped hidden-state intervention, not complete information restoration or causal localization. Incomplete recovery cannot prove that the patched representation lacks information or that earlier layers are unnecessary. Document these bypass paths in metric definitions. Joint gate-input interventions, if implemented and budgeted, must be reported separately with precisely specified positions and paths rather than replacing the original summaries. Missing donors remain unavailable, not zero effect.

Repair manifest source inspection by recording an explicit architecture/configuration description when inspect.getsource fails; include the fallback and failure reason, and do not label it verified source recovery. Never claim predictor parity without checking the exported predictor. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; this proposal needs only histories. Reviews, ratings, item categories, prices, stores and simulator diversity/conformity traits are unavailable. Treat qualitative immediate-fit and stale-interest complaints as user-observed failure hypotheses, not semantic labels inferred from corruption tests.

Overfitting and shortcuts: all gates are learned from the same next-item targets and may overfit item identity, become static, or amplify popularity correlations already in the backbone. A direct embedding path is not by itself evidence of shortcut learning. Keep the baseline regularization unchanged for the first contrast, limit validation-driven variants in advance, and disclose validation reuse. Compare static/current-item/recent-context controls where affordable and summarize gate variation across histories descriptively; variable gates alone do not establish useful adaptation. Host validation decides benchmark improvement, while simulator feedback can describe immediate-fit failures without being treated as direct evidence about unobserved ownership or compatibility. The untouched host final evaluation remains the confirmation step.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
from torch import nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

class RecentContextResidualGate(nn.Module):
    """Attach to an existing completed NextItNet residual update."""
    def __init__(self, hidden_size):
        super().__init__()
        self.proj = nn.Linear(4 * hidden_size, hidden_size)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.proj.weight)
        nn.init.constant_(self.proj.bias, 2.0)

    def forward(self, h, update, item_features, recent_context, mask):
        logits = self.proj(torch.cat(
            [h, update, item_features, recent_context], dim=-1))
        denominator = torch.sigmoid(logits.new_tensor(2.0))
        multiplier = torch.sigmoid(logits) / denominator
        return (h + multiplier * update) * mask.to(h.dtype)


def causal_recent_mean(item_features, sequence, window=4):
    # Features: B x L x H; item IDs: B x L.
    # No target input, future input, or additional L2 normalization.
    if window < 1:
        raise ValueError('window must be positive')
    valid = sequence.ne(0).unsqueeze(-1).to(item_features.dtype)
    masked = item_features * valid
    totals = F.pad(masked.cumsum(dim=1), (0, 0, 1, 0))
    counts = F.pad(valid.cumsum(dim=1), (0, 0, 1, 0))
    ends = torch.arange(1, sequence.size(1) + 1,
                        device=sequence.device)
    starts = (ends - window).clamp_min(0)
    sums = totals[:, ends] - totals[:, starts]
    number = counts[:, ends] - counts[:, starts]
    return (sums / number.clamp_min(1)) * valid


def assert_optimizer_coverage(model, optimizer):
    expected = {id(p) for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad}
    actual = [id(p) for group in optimizer.param_groups
              for p in group['params']]
    assert len(actual) == len(set(actual)), 'duplicate optimizer parameter'
    assert set(actual) == expected, 'missing or unexpected parameter'

# Integration requires the supplied corrected baseline; these helpers are
# not a replacement train.py or a reconstruction of its unspecified API.
# 1. Initialize all existing baseline parameters normally.
# 2. Register one gate per residual block, preserving Torch RNG state.
# 3. Construct the unchanged baseline optimizer after gate registration.
# 4. Assert optimizer parameter coverage exactly once.
#
# Within corrected log2feats(sequence):
#     mask = sequence.ne(0).unsqueeze(-1)
#     e = existing_input_item_embeddings(sequence) * mask
#     c = causal_recent_mean(e, sequence, window=4)
#     h = existing_baseline_input_transform(e)
#     for each existing block:
#         u = existing completed causal residual update, including
#             its existing dropout, before adding h
#         h = block.gate(h, u, e, c, mask)
#     return existing_baseline_final_transform(h), masked as before
# Keep the existing block.forward output B x L x H for diagnostic hooks.
# Train every component jointly with unchanged loss and padding exclusion.
#
# Before training:
#     explicitly copy shared baseline tensors for the neutral-gate check
#     verify feature/logit equivalence in eval mode
#     derive dependency sets through every convolution and gate path
#     verify padding, future invariance and out-of-dependency invariance
#     check finite expected gradients and actual parameter updates
#
# Readout:
#     positions = arange(L) broadcast over batch
#     last = max(where(sequence != 0, positions, -1), dim=1)
#     gather at last for nonempty rows
#     use the existing explicit baseline fallback for empty rows
#
# Export identical architecture code/config through the predictor writer.
# Strictly reload the actual generated predictor and compare eval features,
# candidate scores and rankings for every category route and history case.
# Retain diagnosis APIs and report hidden-state patch bypass paths.
# Select only by pinned host macro validation HR@10.
# Deploy exactly one selected independently trained checkpoint/category.

originality.positive: The particular combination of current-item, recent-composition and residual-update conditioning gives a concrete family-preserving experiment.
originality.negative: Conditional residual modulation and pooled context are established; the recent mean may duplicate information already represented by NextItNet.

future_potential.positive: Controlled comparisons could establish when local composition helps selective modulation while preserving useful ordered histories.
future_potential.negative: Gates may become static or overfit identity correlations, and interaction histories cannot reliably establish immediate intent, ownership or compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: The network modification uses one causal pooling helper and a small linear gate per existing block.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful residual integration, initialization controls, dependency analysis, diagnostic interpretation and actual predictor parity require more work than the small patch suggests.

related_work.title: [1] A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal dilated-convolution residual backbone retained by the proposal.
Preserves ordered context while expanding receptive fields.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed recent-context residual gate or adaptive forgetting.
Provides no evidence for this modification on the pinned four-category benchmark.

related_work.title: [2] Hierarchical Gating Networks for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides precedent for feature-level and instance-level selection in sequential recommendation.
limitations: Does not validate neutral-initialized gating of completed NextItNet residual updates.
Gating does not establish user intent, ownership or product compatibility.

related_work.title: [3] Wu et al.: sampled-softmax recommendation study, TOIS 2024
contributions: Supports investigating sampled-softmax objectives and temperature-dependent hard-negative emphasis.
Motivates a separate objective direction for candidate discrimination.
limitations: Does not demonstrate gains for this NextItNet gate or host benchmark.
Excessive sharpening can concentrate gradients on a few difficult negatives.

related_work.title: [4] Highway Networks
contributions: Establishes input-dependent transform and carry gates as an architectural precedent.
limitations: Coupled transform/carry gating differs from preserving the additive skip and scaling only its residual.
Does not validate this recommendation application.

related_work.title: [5] ReZero is All You Need: Fast Convergence at Large Depth
contributions: Uses learned input-independent residual scales initialized at zero.
Clarifies the distinction between initially suppressing a residual branch and preserving a baseline residual computation.
limitations: Does not provide input-conditioned residual selection.
Zero initialization gives different initial residual-parameter gradients from the proposed multiplier-one initialization.

related_work.title: [6] Going Deeper with Image Transformers
contributions: Introduces LayerScale, using input-independent per-channel residual scales initialized near zero.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed causal conditioning mechanism.
Its initialization attenuates initial residual contributions rather than preserving the supplied NextItNet block.

related_work.title: [7] How Powerful are Graph Neural Networks?
contributions: Explains expressive differences between mean and sum aggregation of multisets.
Supports the distinction between relative composition and multiplicity-sensitive aggregation.
limitations: Its graph-learning results do not establish recommendation gains.
Sum pooling of arbitrary learned embeddings does not guarantee recovery of individual item counts; at fixed window size it is a rescaling of mean pooling.

related_work.title: [8] Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Shows that corruption methods, intervention choices and outcome metrics materially affect activation-patching conclusions.
Motivates explicit reporting of intervention scope and surviving dependency paths.
limitations: Does not directly validate these NextItNet diagnostics.
Hidden-state interventions with active embedding-to-gate paths cannot establish complete information restoration or causal localization.

related_work.title: PyTorch Conv1d documentation
contributions: Documents convolution kernel, dilation, stride and padding semantics needed for causal dependency calculations.
limitations: Correct individual convolution settings do not establish whole-network causality; gate, normalization and residual paths also require checks.

related_work.title: PyTorch: Saving and Loading Models
contributions: Supports saving state dictionaries, reconstructing the matching architecture and switching to evaluation mode.
limitations: Serialization alone does not establish equality between training and generated predictor implementations; explicit parity checks remain necessary.

related_work.title: PyTorch Adam documentation
contributions: Documents optimizer parameter groups and adding parameters after optimizer construction.
limitations: Does not automatically detect omitted or duplicate trainable parameters; this experiment registers gates before optimizer construction and checks coverage explicitly.
